messages:
marco: Escalation from AcmeCorp — their streaming chat endpoints truncate after ~65s idle when routed through ALB + Cloudflare. Customer sees a few SSE events then the connection closes with no 5xx from our app. Repro steps, traces, and app logs below. Please triage and advise next steps.

ava: Thanks — can you confirm if this path is HTTP/2 or HTTP/1.1? Also what's the ALB idle timeout and are they on proxied Cloudflare (orange cloud) or DNS only? Any client library info?

marco: They're on Cloudflare proxied (orange), ALB fronting the origin (target group -> EC2 autoscaled). Client is a browser SPA using EventSource. Repro curl I ran from our corp box: 
```
curl -N -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://acme.example.com/stream?chat_id=..."
```
Server logs (excerpt):
```
[2025-07-03T14:22:11.102Z] stream: started  id=abc123
[2025-07-03T14:23:16.214Z] stream: wrote event chunk size=512 id=abc123
[2025-07-03T14:23:16.215Z] upstream: writev() failed (32: Broken pipe) while sending to client, client: 10.0.0.45:53412
[2025-07-03T14:23:16.215Z] stream: ended unexpectedly id=abc123
```
No application error prior to writev. Packet capture summary attached: ALB sends FIN then RST at ~65s after last activity.

mike: ALB default idle timeout is 60s (user changed?), Cloudflare has its own timeouts (100s for proxied HTTP?), combining proxies can cause midstream half-close behavior. Also check whether HTTP/2 multiplexing + ALB might idle upstream connection and tear down. Do we see gRPC or HTTP/2 between CF and ALB?

ava: Quick debugging suggestions:
- Try reproducing with curl forcing http/1.1: `curl -N --http1.1 -H "Accept: text/event-stream" ...`
- Bypass Cloudflare (temporarily change host header or use the origin's public IP via /etc/hosts) to see if ALB alone cuts.
- If nginx/Envoy sits as reverse proxy, set `proxy_buffering off; proxy_set_header Connection "";` and add `X-Accel-Buffering: no` from the app so upstream proxies don't buffer SSE.
Example nginx snippet we asked customer to try on origin: 
```
proxy_buffering off;
proxy_cache off;
proxy_http_version 1.1;
proxy_set_header Connection "";
```
And for app responses: `res.setHeader('X-Accel-Buffering','no')` and ensure Transfer-Encoding: chunked.

marco: They tried forcing HTTP/1.1 and disabling nginx buffering — still reproduced when Cloudflare in front. When Cloudflare bypassed and we hit ALB directly the stream stayed alive > 5 minutes. So seems Cloudflare+ALB interaction. PCAP shows Cloudflare sends FIN then ALB sends FIN->RST.

sre-bot: Created INC-1234 for customer-facing incident.

mike: Next step: bisect where the tear-down originates. Two toggles: (A) Pause Cloudflare proxying (DNS bypass) -> already did, looks fine. (B) Try switching ALB to TCP mode (NLB) to remove HTTP/1.1/idle-timeout translation and see if connection persists. Also request Cloudflare support trace (ray id) and ask them for proxy logs.

ava: Short-term mitigation options for customer: implement SSE heartbeat/comment every 25–30s (`: keepalive\n\n`) from the server — browsers EventSource tolerates comments and they prevent idle from being hit. Also make client reconnect logic resilient (auto reconnect with backoff). We'll document these as a supported workaround while Cloudflare investigates.

elaine: I'll loop in eng-runtime to check if our runtime can be emitting a final TCP FIN when KV cache is stale or connection is recycled. mike, can you share ALB access logs + target group health events and the pcap?

mike: Yep attaching ALB logs and pcap via zendesk. For Cloudflare I asked customer for the Ray ID + edge timestamps. If CF confirms they're closing, their team suggested they sometimes close idle HTTP/2 streams earlier when multiplexed and the backend isn't actively writing. Workaround on CF side: enable 'Origin Keepalive' or adjust proxy buffering settings (they have no direct knob for SSE).

marco: Customer pushed heartbeat patch (server sends `:hb\n\n` every 20s) and confirmed streams remain stable behind CF for an hour — good stopgap. They want permanent fix (CF/ALB config or move to direct NLB).

ava: Plan: 1) Ask customer to test direct NLB -> if stable, recommend NLB or ALB change + CF escalation. 2) We'll keep heartbeat as documented workaround. 3) eng-runtime to audit connection lifecycle on sidecars. 4) Follow up with Cloudflare with Ray ID and pcap.

mike: Opening eng-runtime ticket RT-4567 and scheduling a short async sync. I'll update INC-1234 with our findings and recommended OOB config options.

marco: Thanks all — I'll update customer with the NLB test plan and the heartbeat workaround. :thumbsup:
